name: Incident-response whole-body and thyroid gamma monitoring with a Stirling-cooled coaxial HPGe radionuclide identifier (crystal at liquid-nitrogen temperature without liquid nitrogen)
plain_name: Check people for swallowed or inhaled radioactivity after an incident with a portable electrically cooled germanium detector
description: After a radiological incident, an ORTEC Detective portable radionuclide identifier, whose ~50 mm x 30 mm coaxial hyper-pure germanium crystal is cooled electrically by a low-power Stirling cooler (no liquid nitrogen, important for transport), is calibrated and used as a rapidly deployable whole-body and I-131 thyroid monitor running about 3 h on its internal battery. Germanium detectors must be operated at liquid-nitrogen temperature (77 K) in an evacuated cryostat.
keywords: Check people for swallowed or inhaled radioactivity after an incident with a portable electrically cooled germanium detector

sources.citation: HPA-RPD-045 The Use of a High-resolution Radionuclide Identifier as a Portable Whole Body Monitor (M J Youngman, Health Protection Agency, 2008)
Environmental Radioactivity Measuring Methods No.7: Gamma-ray Spectrometry using Germanium Semiconductor Detector (Nuclear Regulation Authority, Japan; amendment June 2021)

requirements.rationale: The germanium crystal must be held at liquid-nitrogen temperature, 77 K.
Deployment by one person in an ordinary car relies on electrical Stirling cooling; liquid nitrogen is explicitly not used.
The germanium crystal sits in an evacuated cryostat; loss of cryostat vacuum degrades the detector.
The cold crystal must be biased and read out by the integral acquisition electronics, so electrical connections to the cooled element are needed.
The monitor ran about 3 h on its internal battery in the field (8 h with the external battery).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
